experiment: long-horizon basin harvest across the committed native seed portfolio
question: does the accumulated descent machinery (mode-11 settle prelude + mode-17 vacancy-transport walks, salted target ladder) pull ANY native x86_64 basin materially below the seed11 record of 176.591 mm, and how does basin yield scale?
method: for each portfolio basin: extract boundaryProjectionTreatment.finalPlacements into a pinned parent fixture; chain mode 11 until stall, then mode 17 walks with target = best+0.8+salt*0.001; accept only fresh fingerprints with strictly lower independent depth; stop after 8 consecutive stalls or 30 hops. Driver mirrors docs/experiments/persistent-vacancy-descent/run-descent.py semantics (fail-closed on crash).

basins.note: measured in the prior virgin-basin experiment (target ladder 178.000+salt)

conclusion: Six independent native basins measured (incl. seed11): per-basin yield is bounded in 0.299-0.614 mm and does not scale with additional salted budget; no native basin reaches 176.5 mm. Combined with the mode-18 certificate and the well-walling result, this closes the long-horizon-harvest hypothesis: better complete layouts require a structurally different CONSTRUCTOR, not more descent budget on pipeline basins.
